blocks.title: Refrigerator
blocks.text: A refrigerator is a device which maintains the temperature of a body below that of its surroundings. It operates in a cyclic process but in reverse to that of the heat engine (Fig. 6.10): a refrigerator absorbs heat from a cold reservoir and gives it off to a hot reservoir. This shows that in a refrigerator the work is done on the system, while in a heat engine work is done by the system.

A refrigerator works on the basis of the Clausius statement of the second law of thermodynamics, as a heat engine operating in reverse. Heat Q_C is drawn from the low-temperature reservoir (LTR) by a compressor and thrown into the high-temperature reservoir (HTR) with the help of external work done. The heat rejected to the HTR, Q_H, is given by Q_C + W = Q_H, or W = Q_H - Q_C. The main purpose of a refrigerator is to extract as much heat Q_C as possible from the LTR with the expenditure of as little work W as possible.
Coefficient of performance of a refrigerator

blocks.title: Coefficient of performance
blocks.text: The ratio of the heat removed from the LTR (Q_C) to the work done (W) is called the coefficient of performance of a refrigerator. A better refrigerator removes a greater amount of heat from inside the refrigerator for the expenditure of a smaller mechanical work or electrical energy: E = Q_C / W = Q_C / (Q_H - Q_C). In terms of temperature, where Q is proportional to T, E = T1 / (T2 - T1), T1 being the temperature of the cold reservoir and T2 that of the hot reservoir.

blocks.title: Example 6.4
blocks.text: A refrigerator has a coefficient of performance 8. If the temperature in the freezer is -23 degrees C, what is the temperature at which it rejects the heat? Solution: E = 8; temperature of the cold reservoir (freezer) T1 = -23 degrees C = -23 + 273 = 250 K; temperature of the hot reservoir (room) T2 = ?. Coefficient of performance E = T1/(T2 - T1); substituting, 8 = 250/(T2 - 250), or 8 (T2 - 250) = 250, or T2 - 250 = 250/8, or T2 = 31.25 + 250 = 281.25 K = 8.25 degrees C.

It takes heat Q2 from the cold side, receives work W from an electric motor, and gives out heat Q1 = Q2 + W to the surroundings. A note says heat does not flow from cold to hot by itself.
blocks.caption: A refrigerator moves heat from the cold compartment to the warmer surroundings using work (original diagram after Figure 6.10).

blocks.prompt: A refrigerator extracts 1200 J from its interior and releases 1800 J to the surroundings each cycle; find the work input and the coefficient of performance (numerical 6.5). Does a refrigerator violate the second law by moving heat from cold to hot (short question 6.7)?
blocks.explanation: W = Q_H - Q_C = 1800 - 1200 = 600 J; E = Q_C/W = 1200/600 = 2. No: the Clausius statement forbids heat flowing from cold to hot by itself; the refrigerator moves it only with external work, and the total entropy of the system plus surroundings still increases.

items: Refrigerator: a heat engine in reverse (Clausius); Q_C taken from the cold compartment, W done on the system, Q_H = Q_C + W rejected to the surroundings. Coefficient of performance E = Q_C/W = Q_C/(Q_H - Q_C) = T1/(T2 - T1). Example 6.4: T2 = 281.25 K = 8.25 degrees C.
